distance_note: Sited near Agua Vista Park on Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 270m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature -- versus roughly 1,000m from Mission Rock's tracked footprint. The City's 2018 environmental review places the project area at the former Pier 64, which the Port's Waterfront Land Use Plan documents call "Pier 64½". Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay rather than tracked because it is a Port/WETA transit facility, not a Mission Bay OCII development block.
summary: A WETA/Port of San Francisco ferry terminal on Terry A. Francois Blvd near Agua Vista Park, in the Mission Bay/Central Waterfront area. The Port's undated project page lists "2025 Phase 2a Marine Demolition and Mattress (complete)" and "2026/2027 Phase 2b Mission Bay Ferry Landing and Agua Vista Park (in progress)"; the San Francisco County Transportation Authority (SFCTA) said on April 28, 2026 that completion is expected by the end of 2027 (an expected date). The City's 2018 environmental review covers it together with a separate water taxi landing about 400 feet to the south.

milestones.text: The Port's project page lists "2025 Phase 2a Marine Demolition and Mattress (complete)" (the page is undated, so the completion date is not known; SFCTA, April 28, 2026, describes the earlier work as "the removal of former Pier 64 and other underwater preparatory work").

The Port's project schedule, read on this date (the page is undated), lists "2026/2027 Phase 2b Mission Bay Ferry Landing and Agua Vista Park (in progress)" after three phases marked "(complete)"; SFCTA, April 28, 2026, says the Port "has completed earlier phases of construction" and that its Prop L funds "will support the installation of piles, gangways, fixed piers, canopies, utilities, and landside improvements". This date is when the page was read, not when Phase 2b began.

SFCTA Board approves $4.5M in Prop L sales-tax funds toward what SFCTA calls "a new $77.1 million ferry landing" (its share of $9.8M approved for three projects; approved April 14, final approval April 28, 2026). This is a funding allocation, not a construction cost; SFCTA's June 2024 five-year program gives a different total project cost of $82,450,000 (see open questions).
Completion of the ferry landing is expected by the end of 2027.

costs.what: SFCTA Board-approved Prop L sales tax funds toward what SFCTA calls "a new $77.1 million ferry landing" (the ferry landing's share of $9.8 million approved for three projects; an allocation, not a construction cost; SFCTA's June 2024 five-year program table gives a total project cost of $82,450,000)

facts.value: A two-berth Ferry Landing for regional ferries and a separate two-berth Water Taxi Landing about 400 feet south (2018 design)
The City's 2018 environmental review places the project area at the former Pier 64, called "Pier 64½" in the Port's Waterfront Land Use Plan documents.
Ferry Landing float 135 x 42 ft, gangway 85 x 10 ft; Water Taxi float 65 x 16 ft (2018 design, not confirmed built)

details.text: Project scope: the City's Final Mitigated Negative Declaration (June 2018, Case No. 2017-008824ENV) treats both landings as one project under a single environmental review; each is a single float with two berths, and the Water Taxi Landing is about 100 feet south of the existing Agua Vista Park fishing pier (2018 design).

Structure sizes, full list from the City's 2018 design (Final Mitigated Negative Declaration, June 2018): Ferry Landing connecting ramp 26 x 22 ft, pier 108 x 22 ft, gangway 85 x 10 ft, float 135 x 42 ft; Water Taxi Landing platform 20 x 10.5 ft, gangway 80 x 6.2 ft, float 65 x 16 ft. Not confirmed as built or as currently planned.

open_questions: Whether the Port's draft Five-Year CIP line item "Pier 64 Sediment Cleanup" covers the same area as this project is not established by the sources read; the City's 2018 environmental review places the project area at the former Pier 64.

Whether Phase 2b is already under way is stated differently by two sources: the Port's undated project page lists it as "(in progress)", while SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post says its Prop L funds "will support the installation of piles, gangways, fixed piers, canopies, utilities, and landside improvements", which reads as work still ahead. The record's "under construction" status rests on the completed earlier phases and the Port's "in progress"; no source dates the start of Phase 2b.

The project's total is stated differently across sources: SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post says "a new $77.1 million ferry landing", while SFCTA's Prop L five-year prioritization program (approved June 25, 2024) shows a total project cost of $82,450,000 ($4,500,000 Prop L and $77,950,000 other funds; construction $74,330,000). Neither is reconciled here, and only the $4.5M Prop L allocation (April 2026) is recorded as a cost figure. Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): this record earlier gave the allocation as $9.8M, which is the total SFCTA approved for three projects.
The structure sizes and positions here are from the City's 2018 design. No later site plan was found, so whether the design changed before construction is not established.

Exact construction start and phase-by-phase dates for Phase 2b (ferry landing plus upland improvements) beyond the year-end-2027 expected completion are not established here; the Port's page lists Phase 2b as "in progress" without a start date.
